summary: This Dockerfile creates an Ubuntu container with git and git-delta (a fancy diff viewer) pre-installed and configured. It sets up a demo git repository with a JavaScript file that has an uncommitted change, so users can immediately see git-delta in action when they run `git diff`. The container also customizes the shell prompt to show a whale emoji, making it clear you're inside a container.

explanations.3: This tells Ubuntu's package installer to run non-interactively, so it won't prompt you for input during the build — it just assumes 'yes' to everything.
explanations.7: Ubuntu's Docker image doesn't include all available software repositories by default. This line adds 'universe' and 'multiverse' to the list of repositories so we can install git-delta, which isn't in the default 'main' repository.
explanations.13: After installing packages, we delete the cached package lists to make the image smaller — they're no longer needed once installation is done.
explanations.29: This creates a demo directory, navigates into it, and then chains multiple commands together using `&&`, so if any command fails, the rest won't run.
explanations.31:
This writes a multi-line JavaScript function into a file using `printf` with escape sequences like `
` for newlines.
explanations.34: This modifies the file we just committed, but doesn't commit the change — so when you run the container and type `git diff`, you'll see the difference between the committed version and this modified version.
explanations.39: This appends a custom prompt string to the bash configuration file. The prompt will display a whale emoji, then the username and current directory, making it visually obvious you're in a container.
explanations.41: This runs bash in interactive mode (`-i`), so when you start the container, you get a shell prompt you can type into instead of the container exiting immediately.
